Antioxidants: Flaxseeds contain lignans, which are antioxidant compounds that may have cancer-fighting properties.
Complete Protein: Eggs are a high-quality source of complete protein, meaning they contain all nine essential amino acids your body can’t produce alone.
Healthy Fats: While eggs contain fats, most are unsaturated, especially if you eat them without the yolk.
Plant-Based Diets: Flaxseed is ideal for vegans or anyone avoiding animal products, as it provides a plant-based source of healthy fats and fibre.
Flaxseed is healthier in terms of providing healthy fats (omega-3s), fibre, and antioxidants.
Eggs are better for providing complete protein, vitamin B12, and specific other nutrients that flaxseed doesn’t provide.
1000 grams (1 kilo) ÷ 5 grams (per tablespoon) = 200 tablespoons of ground flaxseed.
200 tablespoons of ground flaxseed ÷ 1 tablespoon per egg = 200 egg replacements.
So, 1 kilo of ground flaxseed will equal about 200 egg replacements.

ingredients: 75g golden syrup (or honey for a twist)

Maple Syrup offers a richer, more distinct flavour and is great for a subtle difference in taste.
Corn Syrup: Light corn syrup is the closest in texture, though it lacks the caramel-like flavour of golden syrup.
Agave Nectar is a healthier, mild-flavoured option, but it’s a bit sweeter, so you may want to use slightly less.
Molasses: For a deeper, richer flavour, though it’s stronger and darker, use sparingly.
Brown Sugar Syrup: You can make your own by dissolving brown sugar in water and boiling it until it thickens.
